text:
emily: Hey team — just got an escalation from AcmeCorp. After yesterday's canary rollout (models:v2.3.1 -> model-rl-1), their generated README snippets are coming back with broken markdown. Missing closing fences and some stray tokens like: `␀STOP` and `@@` inserted between code blocks. Customer example pasted below. cc @raj @mia :eyes:

emily: customer prompt:
```
Generate a short README section with a fenced bash example and a header
```

emily: expected output (from v2.3.0):
```
### Quickstart
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
```

emily: actual output (v2.3.1 canary):
```
### Quickstart
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
@@
␀STOP
```

emily: customer is understandably upset — formatting is critical for this use case (docs generator). They flagged 8 requests with this pattern overnight.

mia: Thanks @emily. Can you attach request IDs or examples? Also which region/route?

emily: shared 3 request IDs in thread DM and said route: `/v1/generate` model `model-rl-1` region `us-west-2` and content-type `application/json`. all from the same org.

raj: oncall here. seeing deploy-bot triggered canary for models:v2.3.1 at 2025-11-03T02:12:05Z? @deploy-bot can you dump the rollout metadata?

deploy-bot: Canary started: models:v2.3.1 -> model-rl-1 (canary 10% traffic). Rollout ID: r-20251103-221. Targets: prod-us-west-2. Autoscaling: disabled for canary.

jules: pinging runtime team. Two hypotheses: stop-sequence normalization code got tweaked, or tokenization/serialization change for fenced code blocks. We had a change in token escape heuristics in v2.3.1 (PR #4876) that touched delimiter sanitization.

raj: can we repro locally with the same prompt? if yes, collect token-level output (raw tokens) and the final string. also need the raw model logits for a few steps if possible.

mia: repro steps i used:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model":"model-rl-1",
    "prompt":"Generate a short README section with a fenced bash example and a header",
    "max_tokens":120,
    "stop":["\n```", "\n###"],
    "stream":false
  }'
```

mia: output (raw):
```
### Quickstart
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
@@
\u0000STOP
```
```

mia: note the extra `\u0000` and `@@` literal tokens before the final fence. also we see double closing fences in the raw output (````) in some runs which then get collapsed by our postprocessor into a single fence but leave the junk.

jules: thanks — that `\u0000` (NUL) is interesting. PR #4876 had a line that strips nonprintables, but we also added a tiny escape/unescape cycle for safety. i'm worried the unescape path is running twice, turning escaped fence markers into partial tokens.

raj: can you grep logs for `unescape` and `stop_seq` around rollout id r-20251103-221?

jules: running quick grep on canary logs (snippet):
```
[2025-11-03T02:12:07Z] rollout=r-20251103-221 component=tokenizer msg="apply_escape=true"
[2025-11-03T02:12:07Z] rollout=r-20251103-221 component=postproc msg="unescape_applied=true count=2"
[2025-11-03T02:12:08Z] rollout=r-20251103-221 component=postproc msg="stop_sequence_normalize=true"
[2025-11-03T02:12:09Z] rollout=r-20251103-221 component=output msg="emitting fence: ``` -> token_seq[286,287]"
```

jules: looks like postproc applied unescape twice for some requests. repro local: when run with `--apply-escape=false` i don't see the stray NUL or @@.

mia: customer-facing ask: can we rollback or route their org to v2.3.0? they want immediate fix, doc generation pipeline is broken.

raj: ops, can we hot-fix routing for that org to the previous model variant?

ops-bot: Routing change request received. To execute need approval + config id. Approving internal bypass for org `acmecorp` -> model: `model-rl-1:v2.3.0`. Executing in 2m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

support-bot: Priority=P0. Adding to incident. Notifying CSM and C-suite slack channel.

emily: thanks. i've sent the workaround to AcmeCorp (they'll switch their route to pinned v2.3.0 for now). They asked for ETA on permanent fix.

jules: plan: revert the double-unescape in postproc and add a regression test that generates fenced code with stop sequences containing fences. target patch and canary today. if rollback of PR #4876 is faster, do that.

raj: will need a token-level diff and a small repro script we can run in CI. @jules can you paste minimal repro snippet so support/devs can validate quickly?

jules: minimal repro script (python):
```
from redwood_sdk import Client
c = Client(api_key="$DEV")
resp = c.generate(model="model-rl-1", prompt="Generate a short README section with a fenced bash example and a header", max_tokens=120, stop=["\n```","\n###"], stream=False, return_raw_tokens=True)
print(resp.raw_tokens)
print(resp.text)
```

jules: expected fix: ensure unescape path idempotent, and postproc only runs unescape once. I'll open an internal PR and tag `fix/stopseq-unescape`.

mia: thanks. customer wants timeline — can you give an ETA?

jules: aiming for patch + canary within 4 hours. if canary looks good, full deploy end of day. if not, we keep routing org to v2.3.0 until next morning.

emily: customer confirmed the temporary pin to v2.3.0 restored formatting in 3 sampled outputs. they're calmer but want postmortem and compensatory credit. i'll open a support ticket for billing credit.

raj: good. once PR is up ping here. also add the regression test to the serve/formatting suite.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-20251103-14. Severity: P0. Affected orgs: 1 (AcmeCorp).

emily: moving thread to follow-up after fix. thanks all. :heart:
